facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old woman
a history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma
abdominal and pelvic pain
Physical examination was unremarkable
a creatinine level of 0.81 mg dl–1
within normal limits
a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation located in the upper pole
creating a defect in the renal parenchyma

concepts.why: The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, known as a renal parenchymal vascular pedicle, supports the diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma.
The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation is consistent with clear cell renal cell carcinoma, a subtype of renal cell carcinoma.
The presence of a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava supports the diagnosis of renal vein thrombosis.
The patient's history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma supports the diagnosis of this condition.

The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava, in a patient with a history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, raises the possibility of metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

The presence of visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, known as a renal parenchymal vascular pedicle, and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to its confluence with the inferior vena cava, supports the diagnosis of a vascular tumor.
The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation is consistent with renal angiomyolipoma, a benign renal tumor.
The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation is consistent with renal oncocytoma, a benign renal tumor.

rationales.F02: History of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma increases the likelihood of metastatic disease, including to the kidney.
rationales.F07: The presence of a renal mass with fat attenuation is highly suggestive of renal cell carcinoma or angiomyolipoma.
rationales.F09: The presence of a renal parenchymal vascular pedicle is highly suggestive of a renal tumor, particularly renal cell carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of a fatty tumor thrombus in the renal vein is highly suggestive of renal cell carcinoma with venous invasion.
